title: How a block of ice becomes a fridge
lines: Put a block of ice in a wooden box. Congratulations, you've built a fridge.
But by tomorrow, the ice is a puddle, and your milk is cottage cheese.
You need something colder than ice, that never runs out.
So you run a pipe inside, filled with a liquid that boils below freezing.
As it boils, it sucks the heat out of your milk. This is the evaporator.
But once that liquid boils into gas, it just floats away.
So you catch the gas and squeeze it with a pump. This is the compressor.
But squeezing gas makes it hot, just like a bicycle pump.
So you snake that hot pipe down the back. It cools, and turns back into liquid. This is the condenser.
That's why the back of your fridge feels warm.
But that liquid is still warm, and squeezed too tight to boil.
So you push it through a tube thinner than spaghetti. This is the capillary tube.
Like a spray can, the pressure drops, and it goes freezing cold.
But now the loop never stops, and your milk freezes solid.
So a sensor switches the pump off just above freezing. This is the thermostat.
That's the hum that randomly stops and starts.
But every time you open the door, wet air freezes onto the pipes, and the cooling stops.
So a little heater melts it, and the water drips onto the hot pump and dries up.
Here's the twist. It never made cold. It just moves heat from your milk into your kitchen.
Wrap it all in foam and steel. Congratulations, you've built a fridge. Or, you could just...
